title: Nobody cares about all these "fantastic" updates while this game is a money parasite

posts.cooked:
I sometimes see updates here and there about this game. I played it in the past but quit as paying a never ending subscription cannot be justified in my mind when there are so many other - better things to spend money on when the economy is in the gutter like it is.
Therefore, i will say as i have said before. If you want more players to return, you need to stop living in 2018 and modernise your pricing model to reflect the modern world today.
One suggestion would be to let people play with the skills that they have trained - without restrictions and stop being money hungry clowns.
It is common knowledge that their server upkeep costs have been insignificant as to what they spend their money on (executive bonus ect). No thank you.

it does reflect the pricing model of today.

Everquest - $14.99 / Month + $5 of extra perks = total sub cost $20 / month.
Wow - $14.99 / Month
FFXIV - $14.99 / Month
LOTRO - $14.99 / Month
ESO - $14.99 / Month

all of these mmos charge extra for each expansion release. you have to pay anywhere from $30 to $150+ for their expansions and or collectors editions of those expansions.

all of these mmos are cheaper if you buy subscription time in years at a time, they all drop to around $10 / Month. if you sub for 12months in one go.

currently only og Everquest is charging around $20 for a month sub same as Eve (with the added perks) this game is about 5 years older than Eve and isn't gaining that many new players either at this stage. still not magically cheaper because of that though. the age of the game or the number of people playing it doesn't lower the subscription cost. doesn't seem to have any impact at all really.

the unfortunate part about subscriptions in general is the savings are only passed on to those who can afford to get a 1 year sub each time they sub, for practically every subscription service like this (not just mmos or games), its the people doing month by month that pay the most. even though they are likely the ones that need the savings the most. (or have the least amount of money to spend on subscriptions) but it has always been this way. the only thing you can do is wait for sales and buy sub time during a sale.

Perhaps, but there is only 1 Eve. so they can charge what they like for it.

I think Eve is one of the easier mmos to sub for 'free' in though. for example grinding out a wow token in wow without affecting your own progression is difficult to do unless you play every day. In Eve you can passively grind out a second month of omega during your normal gameplay, without it affecting your character progression.

its easier to turn being subbed for 1 month into 2 months or 3 months in Eve than it is in other mmos, assuming you have the skills already or are in a lucrative area of space you can grind out a month of omega (500 plex) in around 20hours at 100m/isk hr.

trying to do the same in say wow would probably take longer, in the EU a wow token is like around 400k gold, if each quest gives you around 2k gold (they don't) and it takes you 20 minutes to do each one, you're looking at it being around 200 quests, taking around 66 hours.

then none of that gold is going into gear or enchantments or gems or consumables. its just letting you play for another month. the time you spend doing stuff in Eve holds its value for longer. a ship you bought 6 months ago is probably worth about the same today.

well fun is subjective, if its not fun then you should probably find something that is fun. I wouldn't play a game I don't find fun. regardless of the subscription cost, it could be $1 a month but i'm not spending that if I don't find the game fun to begin with.

it is an mmo, you're meant to be doing things with other people so that its less of a boring grind and more effcient with your time, besides that its more fun to talk to people while grinding in Eve than it is to sit in silence by yourself. the Pve has always been a bit So-so if you prefer the Pvp then the Pve gets a bit dull but it is there to fill the time between CTAs.

personally I would prefer to just sell plex for my ISK than to grind it out, its just better for me on hours, spending 20+ hours doing level 4s vs spending 1 hr at work, if I grind its usually for the items and materials rather than the raw ISK.

If the value proposition isn't there for you, then it's not there for you. It's time to move on at that point. Like for example, I don't subscribe to OF creators, because the value proposition just isn't there for me. I don't go on OF Reddits to complain that foot pics should cost fifty cents instead of twenty-five dollars. I could, because it's not illegal to complain, but I simply realize the futility of it, because I know that there are plenty of people out there who will dump whatever is left of their paycheck after paying rent every month on OF content. Likewise, EVE is unlikely to become cheaper, because there are enough people out there willing to drop $300 on their fifteen-account ISK-faring setup every month to keep the current business model profitable. They're not going to change it on the assumption that turning EVE into some kind of budget freemo game option is going to bring in this mythical horde of new players to the game that would make them even more money.
Originally posted by Bright New Day (光明新日):

if I was shilling for the game I wouldn't have told you to not play the game that you yourself said was boring.

you'd think the idea of shilling would be to convince people that, yes actually dispite you saying you don't find the game fun, you should continue to sink your time and money into it.

while realistically I think its better that people not waste their time being upset over a game that doesn't really interest them. you said yourself in the OP you 'have better things to spend the money on', so then do that. nothing hostile in that, just Eve is less important than things that are more important. there is no need to try to force yourself to enjoy it.

I guess my family isn't going to be fed this week, because I'm most definitely not getting paid for my post that was effectively a direct criticism of the game's monetization strategy.

That's not to say, however, that this is a nuance that these deranged EVE dropouts are able to understand with their kindergarten-level reading comprehension. They're basically the same people as the ones linking obvious AI slop videos to their friends and family and telling them how they "knew the government was out to get them."

There's really no discourse to be had here. Not any more than, say, trying to discuss the finer points of impressionist art with your dog. You have to remember that you're dealing with someone with an IQ in the upper seventies, and that while you're wasting your words on logic and explanations, the only thing they're doing is visualizing the tall glass of ice-cold Coca-Cola they saw in a TV commercial last night.

The world can be cruel sometimes.
